verdict.rationale: Notion clearly supports creating pages and databases alongside project tracking. First-party docs cover creating and updating pages, databases and comments. Community users report using it as a wiki and project tracker together, and as a balance between PM tools and unstructured wikis. However, the evidence never documents the end-user experience of sharing documents or organizing them (permissions, hierarchy, team spaces); first-party proof comes mainly from API and MCP docs and marketing taglines. missing for 10: first-party documentation of shared/collaborative doc editing and sharing permissions, documented organization features (page hierarchy, workspaces/teamspaces) for notes alongside projects, and hands-on corroboration of multi-user collaboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can create and organize shared docs and notes alongside my project work

citations.quote: Bring everything into one system of record.
you can read, create, and update nearly everything in a workspace — pages, databases, users, comments, and more
We have tried to use it as a wiki, project tracker, issue tracker, CRM & spreadsheet.
We use it to keep track of all of our tasks and projects
finds the perfect balance between strict JIRA/PM tools and completely unstructured wikis/text files
